gap_coverage.sentence: No provided method combines multiple template structures with quality-weighted consensus scoring for low-identity targets: TemplateTransfer depends on one template whose mismatches dominate below 30% identity [2], MultiTempl lets low-quality templates vote with equal weight so low-identity precision stays flat [3], and the strongest consensus alternative, ConsenSite, gains its 0.07 precision only from multiple experimental structures of the target itself, unavailable for most prediction targets [4].
What remains open is consensus scoring across template structures, weighted by per-template local quality, and evaluated on targets whose best template is below 30% identity.

contribution_anchors.bullet: We introduce an LQS-weighted multi-template consensus scoring scheme where each candidate pocket is voted on by up to 5 templates (Fig 1).
On the hard subset of SynBench-60 (template identity below 30%), PermaLig reaches 0.61 top-1 pocket precision versus 0.48 for the best single-template baseline (Fig 2).
An ablation on the hard subset attributes +0.09 top-1 precision to consensus scoring over simple template ranking (Fig 2).
